To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
there is a cross-factor relationship of various software engineering approaches and practices versus the practitioner demographics including their work experience, company size and target industry.

the following are true: (1) More experienced practitioners experience challenges more in software engineering phases and tasks; (2), Almost 55% use software size measurement, (3) Waterfall is not used in small companies but Agile is, (4) As company size increase, Spiral increases, but XP decreases, and (5) Agile is favored by practitioners in small-sized companies and in the software industry, whereas Waterfall, spiral, and V model are not favored.

there is a wide spectrum of software engineering practices in the Turkish software industry, and the types of practices and their usage varies based on the practitioner demographics, i.e., their company and project characteristics.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the cross-factor correlation between software engineering practices and demographics of software practitioners.
software engineering practices in the Turkish context.

the cross-factor relationship between software engineering practices and demographics, and the results of the study will help us to better understand this relationship and to identify new research areas.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the results of this explorative study will be useful in identifying the cross-factor relationship between software engineering practices and various practitioner demographics, and thus help practitioners and researchers both in industry and academia.

the results of the study will be useful for practitioners, researchers and educators to identify the types and maturity level of software engineering practices being used in the industry and to pinpoint the special issues which should receive more attention and be studied in the context of different demographics.
there is an urgent need to study the above research directions in the Turkish and world-wide contexts.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have conducted an exploratory study to understand the cross-factors of various software engineering approaches versus practitioner demographics including the company size, sector, and project size.

this study is the first to reveal the cross-factor relationship between software engineering practices and practitioners demographics, and it will be helpful to practitioners and researchers in Turkey and world wide.
the software industry in Turkey is very dynamic and is in the process of adopting new SE practices, tools and methodologies, and that there are many opportunities and challenges in this area.
The main takeaway from our work is that

it is important for software engineering researchers and practitioners to understand the cross-factors of various software engineering approaches and techniques versus practitioner demographics, e.g., what are the best practices and challenges of using software engineering tools in small-sized companies versus large ones?, and how could software engineers in the military sector utilize Agile development approaches?

the software engineering community should conduct similar studies in other countries to get a better understanding of the cross-factor relationship between software engineering practices and demographic factors in each country.
